answer: Agents named cedar, zephyr, and yarrow allocate shared compute through stake-weighted voting: each ballot’s weight equals the tokens its sender has locked in escrow for 30 days, not one vote per account. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand fake agents still buys only 100 tokens of influence. To control a majority, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more stake than all honest voters combined, tying up capital and bearing its price risk.
